method.description: Design reconciliation of one continuation identity against the form it claims to continue. Rule 2.86—Form 2 was read in the Iowa Supreme Court's own order adopting it, and the passage that gives rise to the attached-sheet expectation was located and read verbatim.
method.controllingSource: the Iowa Supreme Court order filed 30 August 2024 amending Chapter 2, which attaches Rule 2.86—Forms 1 to 5 in full; published by the Legislative Service Agency at legis.iowa.gov
method.assignmentConstraintObserved: The stop condition requires preserving the exact not-required reason, including custom pleading versus no participant filing, and forbids collapsing it into source missing or altering an adopted strategy. The reason is recorded precisely, and it is neither of the two branches the stop condition names — a third case is identified rather than forced into one of them.

finding.headline: The attached sheet is real, is expected by the form, and is not a document. Rule 2.86—Form 2 carries a checkbox reading 'Check this box if you have attached a sheet with additional alternate names', and the sheet the participant attaches is their own plain list. The Iowa Judicial Branch prescribes no form for it, and none is needed.
finding.acquisitionRequiredRationale: No issuer interaction can produce a prescribed form for an attachment the rule leaves to the participant to write. Nothing is published and nothing is expected to be.

controllingText.form: Iowa R. Crim. P. 2.86—Form 2, Application to Expunge Misdemeanor Court Records under Iowa Code section 901C.3
controllingText.whereTheAttachedSheetAppears: item 1, Defendant's personal information, immediately after the block for all other names ever used
controllingText.checkboxVerbatim: Check this box if you have attached a sheet with additional alternate names.
controllingText.surroundingContext: The item asks for the defendant's current legal name and then for 'All other names ever used (including any other previous legal names and nicknames)', giving fields for full first, middle and last name. The checkbox follows, providing for the case where the printed fields run out.
controllingText.whatTheRuleSaysAboutTheSheet: Nothing beyond that sentence. Rule 2.86 is titled simply 'Forms' and its entire content is the five forms; it prescribes no attachment format, no heading, no caption and no numbering for the sheet.
controllingText.governingProcedureRule: Rule 2.81 governs the § 901C.3 application and requires only that the application substantially comply with Form 2. It says nothing about an attached sheet.
controllingText.substantialComplianceStandard: Rule 2.81(2) reads that an application 'shall be initiated by executing and filing an application that substantially complies with Rule 2.86—Form 2'. A substantial-compliance standard is itself inconsistent with a prescribed continuation form: if the applicant may vary the application, they may certainly supply a plain list of extra names.

notRequiredReasonPreserved.whyNotNoParticipantFiling: The participant does file. They file the application, and where they have more alternate names than the form's fields allow, they attach their own sheet and tick the box. This is the opposite of the Florida administrative-expunction case resolved in this same shard, where the participant files nothing because the instrument is an agency's.
notRequiredReasonPreserved.whyNotCustomPleading: A custom pleading is a drafted legal document with a caption, allegations and a prayer for relief, produced because no official form exists for a filing that must be made. Here the official form exists, is used, and simply overflows. What overflows is a list of names, not a pleading. Calling it a custom pleading would imply a drafting exercise where the correct output is a list.
notRequiredReasonPreserved.theThirdCase: A participant-supplied free-form attachment. The form anticipates it, provides a checkbox to declare it, and prescribes no format. The right disposition is that no document identity should exist for it at all.
notRequiredReasonPreserved.whyTheDistinctionMatters: Each branch implies different downstream work. No-participant-filing means the component is removed. Custom pleading means a template must be written and a specification drafted. This third case means the component becomes a conditional overflow behaviour on the parent form — no template, no identity, no acquisition, and a small amount of assembly logic.
notRequiredReasonPreserved.adoptedStrategyUnchanged: The track's output strategy is untouched. Whether ia-901c3's continuation component is removed or re-modelled as overflow behaviour is a legal-design decision, and this record supplies the source-side fact it rests on.

resolvedIdentity.roleAssessment: continuation is descriptively right about the function and wrong about the object. Something does continue the name list; it is just not a published document.
resolvedIdentity.recordedIssuingAuthorityAssessment: There is no issuer, because there is no issued document. The Judicial Branch issues Form 2; it does not issue the sheet a participant attaches to it.
resolvedIdentity.parentFormRetained: the queue records that Rule 2.86 Form 2 is confirmed current at the August 2024 revision and is retained by Edition 1.2
resolvedIdentity.componentCountNote: The shard manifest records four assigned components for the ia-901c3 track; this identity binds one of them.
resolvedIdentity.scope: not applicable — no document, so no scope

queuePositionAssessed.recordedCurrentnessQuestion: Rule 2.86 Form 2 itself is confirmed current at the August 2024 revision and is retained by Edition 1.2. Whether the attached sheet is a separate published document or a continuation page of Form 2 is unresolved.
queuePositionAssessed.assessment: The question is well posed and the answer is neither of its two alternatives. The attached sheet is not a separate published document, and it is also not a continuation page of Form 2 — Form 2 is three pages and none of them is a spare names page. It is a third thing: a sheet the participant supplies.
queuePositionAssessed.recordedEditionRationale: No separate published binary for an attached sheet was found on the Iowa Judicial Branch forms collection.
queuePositionAssessed.assessmentOfThatRationale: Correct as far as it goes, but stated as a failure to find. This record states the negative affirmatively: the rule text that creates the expectation also shows that nothing is prescribed, so there is nothing to find.

iowaPatternObservation.commonCause: The Iowa normalization appears to have created a document identity for every nameable part of a filing — a section, a packet page, an overflow attachment — rather than for every published document. All three were then recorded as unacquired sources, which sent retrieval work after things that were never separately published.
iowaPatternObservation.recommendation: Worth checking the remaining Iowa identities against the same test before any further Iowa acquisition is scheduled: does the issuer publish this as a file, or is it a part of something else, or is it the participant's own paper?
iowaPatternObservation.notADuplicateFinding: The three resolve differently — a section of a form, a page of a packet, and no document at all — so they are not one finding repeated. Only the originating pattern is shared.

doNotSubstitute.why: The parent application. It is retained and current at August 2024. The attached sheet is not a page of it, and binding the parent to the continuation component would double-emit the application.
The applications for § 901C.2, § 123.46, § 123.47 and § 725.1. Each carries the same alternate-names structure, so each could appear to be the missing sheet. None is.

doNotSubstitute.document: Iowa Ct. R. 17 family-law continuation or additional-page forms
doNotSubstitute.why: Chapter 17 prescribes forms for self-represented litigants in family matters and its use is mandatory there. Nothing in it reaches a criminal expungement application, and importing a Chapter 17 attachment would also import a mandatory-use assumption that does not apply to Rule 2.86.

doNotSubstitute.documentClass: a drafted continuation template produced by this programme
doNotSubstitute.why: It would give a prescribed shape to something the rule deliberately leaves free-form, and would risk a clerk rejecting a filing for using a format the court never adopted.

doNotSubstitute.documentClass: a county clerk's local attachment form
doNotSubstitute.why: A local form is not a statewide instrument and the rule prescribes none.

No implementation job depends on this identity, so nothing is released.
implementationFamilyEffect.familyReadinessStatement: The Iowa official-PDF family remains fail-closed and this job does not move it. The five Rule 2.86 applications are unmanifested and unretrieved behind an iowacourts.gov refusal, the DCI packet mapping is unapproved, generation is not permitted, runtime is disabled and no field map is built.
implementationFamilyEffect.assemblyObservation: If the component is re-modelled as overflow behaviour, the assembly need is small: detect that the alternate-names list exceeds the printed fields, emit a plain continuation sheet of names, and tick the checkbox on the parent. Recorded as an observation; the modelling decision is the legal-design owner's.

terminalDispositionDetail.why: The narrowest disposition the evidence supports. It is not source_missing, which the stop condition forbids and which would be false — nothing is missing, because nothing was ever published. It is not no_participant_filing, because the participant does file and does attach the sheet. It is not custom_pleading, because what is attached is a list of names rather than a drafted legal document. It is not unresolved: the rule text that creates the expectation is the same text that shows nothing is prescribed.

expectedDownstreamEffect: One Iowa acquisition key closes without a download and with its reason recorded as a third case the assignment's own two branches do not cover: the participant files, and what they attach is their own free-form list of alternate names, declared by a checkbox the form provides and prescribed in no format by the rule. The identity is shown to name no published document and is recommended for retirement rather than acquisition, and the recorded issuing authority is identified as wrong because the Judicial Branch does not issue the sheet. The Iowa pattern is named — three identities now resolved as a section, a packet page and a participant attachment — with a test to apply to the rest before further Iowa retrieval is scheduled. No binary is acquired, no receipt is created, nothing enters version control, no adopted strategy is altered, no component is rebound, no template is drafted, no memo is edited, no edition is published, no packet becomes generatable, no runtime is enabled and no track changes promotion state.
